title: Flame Design: radiative extinction and sustained spherical flames
summary: The final report describes atmospheric-pressure ethylene experiments and transient simulations. The flight program used ethylene except for one propane calibration day; proposed methane and CO2-diluent tests were not performed.

title: BRE: quasi-steady burning and extinction boundaries
summary: The final report describes quasi-steady flames at nominal oxygen mole fractions of 0.265 and above in the tested configurations. Normal-atmosphere flames self-extinguished within 40 s, while methane/nitrogen flames extinguished within a minute across the tested atmospheres. Both large-flame radiative extinction and a small-flame quenching limit were identified. These are gas-burner emulation results, not direct burns of every condensed material represented by the model. The desired O2/CO2 atmospheric objective was not tested.

title: s-Flame: radiative and kinetic extinction modes
summary: The report describes nitrogen- and helium-diluted hydrogen, methane and ethylene experiments. In the cited ethylene/nitrogen tests, increasing flow led to radiative extinction and decreasing flow led to kinetic extinction. For the 20–30% ethylene mixtures described on page 26, flames established at 3 cc/s extinguished during ramps before reaching 1 cc/s downward or 8 cc/s upward. These limits describe the reported ramp protocols and are not universal fuel flammability limits. The report states that detailed analysis was ongoing.
